raw_case_text: A 63-year-old married man of Asian ethnicity, on regular haemodialysis three times weekly undergoing diabetic nephropathy for the last two years, was complaining of having walking difficulties for two months. He was known to have chronic hepatitis B liver disease staged Child A with grade I oesophageal varices under anti viral therapy including the combination of lamivudine plus adefovir adjusted to kidney function tests. He also had a history of an operated hepatocellular carcinoma. He had many diabetic degenerative complications (proliferative retinopathy, stented ischemic heart disease, peripheral neuropathy) as well. He started complaining of a symmetrical painful proximal lower limbs weakness attributed initially to lumbar root compression according to lumbar CT scan and EMG/NCS findings. The former showed diffuse degenerative changes associated with a disc protrusion at L3-L4 level. The later showed evidence of a pending left external popliteal sciatic nerve without evidence of diffuse symmetrical polyneuropathy. Symptoms were relieved by benign pain killer and gabapentin 300 mg every other day. Three months later he arrived at the emergency department with mild fever, non productive cough, nocturnal sweat and inability to walk. Physical examination revealed an ill looking patient, weighing 63 kgs with blood pressure of 154/95 mmHg, heart rate 104 bpm regular, temperature 38.2 C and oxygen saturation of 95%. Glasgow score was 15 without meningismus or oto-ocular manifestations. Proprioception was conserved and Babinski, Hoffman and Laseque signs were all negative. The patient had mild walking abnormalities, MSGS at 3/5 and very poor squat test. However, both patellar reflexes were active, and symmetric. He had no pain or peripheral numbness. Cardiovascular examination showed moderate tachycardia without friction rub or murmurs. There were bi-basal crackles mostly on the right side with absence of dullness on percussion and hepatojugular reflux. The peripheral pulse was conserved without acrosyndrom. Skin examination showed pityriasis versicolor-like eruptions mainly on upper limbs and upper thorax. The external genitalia revealed hypochromic vitiligoid spots on the scrotum. He was free of lymphadenopathy. Results of laboratory investigations are shown in tables 1, 2 and 3. Sputum smear for bacterial and mycobacterium, urine C/S, blood C/S (3), Mantoux test, were all negative. iPTH = 205 ng/l (15-65), 1, 25(OH) D3 24 pmol/l (43 - 148) and 25 OH D3 = 38 nmol/l (75 - 200) with normal phosphocalcic product. VDRL = 2, TPHA 1280, FTA abs 100, FTA -M <10 and positive anti -TpN47, TmpA, TpN17 and TpN 15(IgG western-blot). EKG showed no new changes and transthoracic Doppler-echocardiography demonstrated normal left ventricular size and function apart from mild concentric hypertrophy. He had no significant valvulopathy, though a calcified bicuspid aortic valve with mild regurgitation was noted without Aortitis or aneurismal aspects. CXR disclosed an interstitial aspect of both field of the lungs and normal sized mediastinal silhouette. Funduscopic appearance showed beside proliferative retinopathy, a syphilitic uveitis thereafter, discovered incidentally elsewhere. Abdominal and pelvis ultrasound study demonstrated mild splenomegaly and poorly differentiated normal sized kidneys with acquired cystic disease. The patient received an empirical treatment of ceftriaxone 1.5 gr administered post-dialysis with a spectacular response within one week; therapy judged by net improvement of his weakness and return home walking. Ceftriaxone alone was maintained to complete duration of two weeks. Meanwhile, the spouse of the patient was convoked for screening. We learned that she had been receiving prednisolone and sub-cutaneous injection of infliximab weekly for the last six months, and ibuprofen for a relapsing rheumatoid arthritis. Awaited syphilitic serologic testing disclosed normal blood chemistry without inflammation (CRP = 5 mg/l). VDRL = 2, TPPA = 2560 FTA abs 200, FTA-M 20 (N <10). A medical report was sent to her general practitioner for intramuscular Benzathin-penicillin therapy 2.4 Millions units weekly over three consecutive weeks.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 63-year-old Asian man on maintenance hemodialysis presented with a 2-month history of painful proximal lower-limb weakness progressing to inability to walk, mild fever, non-productive cough, and night sweats.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two months prior to admission (3 months before emergency presentation), the patient developed symmetric painful proximal lower-extremity weakness initially attributed to L3-L4 disc protrusion on lumbar CT and left external popliteal sciatic nerve involvement on EMG/NCS, with partial pain relief from analgesics and gabapentin 300 mg every other day. He subsequently presented to the emergency department with inability to walk, mild fever, dry cough, and nocturnal sweats.
subjective.past_medical_history: End-stage diabetic nephropathy on thrice-weekly hemodialysis for 2 years; diabetic proliferative retinopathy, stented ischemic heart disease, and peripheral neuropathy; Child-Pugh class A chronic hepatitis B cirrhosis with grade I esophageal varices on renal-adjusted lamivudine plus adefovir; and prior resected hepatocellular carcinoma. Married; his wife was being treated with prednisolone, weekly subcutaneous infliximab, and ibuprofen for relapsing rheumatoid arthritis.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for proximal leg weakness, inability to walk, low-grade fever, dry cough, and night sweats; negative for meningismus, headache, active leg pain/numbness at ED admission, or oto-ocular complaints. Home medications: lamivudine, adefovir, and gabapentin.

objective.physical_examination: Ill-appearing male weighing 63 kg; blood pressure 154/95 mmHg, heart rate 104 bpm regular, temperature 38.2 C, SpO2 95%, and GCS 15 without meningismus. Neurological exam showed proximal lower-limb weakness (motor score 3/5, poor squat test) with preserved proprioception, symmetric active patellar reflexes, and negative Babinski, Hoffmann, and Lasegue signs. Cardiopulmonary exam showed moderate tachycardia without murmurs/rubs and right-predominant bibasilar pulmonary crackles. Cutaneous and genital exam revealed pityriasis versicolor-like eruptions on the upper limbs and upper thorax, hypochromic vitiligoid macules on the scrotum, and no lymphadenopathy. Fundoscopy showed background diabetic proliferative retinopathy and incidental syphilitic uveitis.
objective.routine_investigations: Sputum smears for bacteria and mycobacteria, 3 blood cultures, urine culture, and Mantoux test were negative. Secondary hyperparathyroidism and vitamin D deficiency were noted: iPTH 205 ng/L (normal 15-65), 1,25(OH)2D3 24 pmol/L (43-148), and 25(OH)D3 38 nmol/L (75-200). Chest X-ray showed bilateral interstitial lung markings; ECG showed no acute changes; TTE showed mild concentric LV hypertrophy and a calcified bicuspid aortic valve with mild regurgitation without aortitis or aneurysm; abdominal/pelvic ultrasound showed mild splenomegaly and acquired cystic kidney disease.
objective.advanced_workup: Prior lumbar CT showed diffuse degenerative changes and L3-L4 disc protrusion; EMG/NCS showed left external popliteal sciatic nerve dysfunction without diffuse symmetric polyneuropathy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed secondary/subacute myopathic and uveitic syphilis in a hemodialysis patient (and latent/secondary syphilis in his immunosuppressed spouse), established via reactive serum VDRL (titer 1:2), positive TPHA (1:1,280), positive FTA-ABS (100, FTA-M <10), and positive IgG Western blot for TpN47, TmpA, TpN17, and TpN15 (spouse also tested positive: VDRL 1:2, TPPA 2,560, FTA-ABS 200, FTA-M 20). Treated with intravenous ceftriaxone 1.5 g administered post-dialysis for 2 weeks, resulting in dramatic recovery of proximal muscle strength and independent ambulation within 1 week; his wife was referred for intramuscular benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units weekly for 3 weeks.
